chapter_note: Chapter is 88% damaged. The opening (segs 5-13) preserves fragments of a four-kingdoms enumeration teaching — substrate, but heavily lacunose. Beginning at seg 14 ("But I say to you in truth"), the chapter pivots entirely to hortatory/ecclesial application: a discourse on the merit of giving bread and drink to disciples and catechumens, the Holy Spirit dwelling in believers, and recompense at the last day. Editorial fatigue score is positive — apostolic_dialogue front-loaded, ecclesial+hortatory dominate the second half. The cosmological "four kingdoms" frame appears to have been used as a launching point for an extended pastoral application about almsgiving to the institutional ranks. Sileus is preserved as a named kingdom-figure.
